{{Short description|French mathematician (1879–1953)}}
'''André Gérardin''' (1879, [[Nancy, France|Nancy]], [[Meurthe-et-Moselle]] – 1953, Nancy, Meurthe-et-Moselle) was a French mathematician, specializing in [[number theory]] and calculating machines used in [[integer factorization|factoring large positive integers]], finding primes, and calculating [[quadratic residue]]s modulo a given positive integer.<ref name=BoyerPreface>{{cite web|title=''Diophante'', English version of preface by Christian Boyer, translated from the French by Jeffrey Shallit, 2005|website=University of Illinois Library|url=https://www.library.illinois.edu/mtx/DiophanteNumberTheoryJournal/DiophanteEnglPreface.pdf}}</ref>

Gérardin became a member of the [[Société Mathématique de France]] in 1906.<ref>{{cite book|title=Gérardin, André (1879–1953)|via=BnF Catalogue général|url=http://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb15076726c}}</ref> He wrote many articles for ''[[L'Enseignement Mathématique]]'', ''[[Nouvelles Annales de Mathématiques]]'', and other French mathematical journals, as well as a few articles for foreign mathematical journals.<ref name=BoyerPreface/> He was one of nine mathematicians who read the initial page proofs and suggested improvements for the first volume of [[Leonard E. Dickson]]'s ''[[History of the Theory of Numbers]]''.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Dickson | first1=Leonard Eugene | title=History of the theory of numbers. Vol. I: Divisibility and primality. | year=1919 | chapter= Preface | page=xii|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.hwsqx8;view=1up;seq=18 | publisher=Carnegie Institute of Washington | location= Washington, D. C.}}</ref> In that volume, Dickson and Gérardin announced for the first time that the [[Mersenne prime|Mersenne number]] M<sub>173</sub> has the factor 730753.<ref>{{cite book|author=Dickson, L. E.|volume=1|page=32|title=History of the theory of numbers|year=1919|publisher=Washington|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.hwsqx8;view=1up;seq=50}}</ref>

Gérardin was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1912 at Cambridge UK,<ref>{{cite book|author=Gérardin, A.|chapter=Répertoire bibliographique des sciences mathématiques|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the Fifth International Congress of Mathematicians (Cambridge, 22–28 August 1912)|pages=444–446|volume=2|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uc1.31822008115719;view=1up;seq=450}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Gérardin, A.|chapter=Note historique sur la théorie des nombres|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the Fifth International Congress of Mathematicians (Cambridge, 22–28 August 1912)|page=539|volume=2|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uc1.31822008115719;view=1up;seq=545}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Gérardin, A.|chapter=Sur quelques nouvelles machines algébriques|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the Fifth International Congress of Mathematicians (Cambridge, 22–28 August 1912)|pages=572–573|volume=2|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uc1.31822008115719;view=1up;seq=578}}</ref> in 1920 at Strasbourg,<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=msu.31293001749500;view=1up;seq=663|pages=613–616|year=1921|title=Compte rendu du Congrès international des mathématiciens tenu à Strasbourg du 22 au 30 Septembre 1920|chapter=''Décomposition des nombres. Jeux scientifiques inédits'' par A. Gérardin}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=msu.31293001749500;view=1up;seq=667|pages=617–620|year=1921|title=Compte rendu du Congrès international des mathématiciens tenu à Strasbourg du 22 au 30 Septembre 1920|chapter=''Machines à congruences. Théorie et pratique'' par A. Gérardin}}</ref> in 1928 at Bologna, and in 1932 at Zürich. He was the founder and editor for many years of the mathematical review ''Sphinx-Oedipe'', started in 1906. In 1944 he, along with Paul Belgodère, started the journal ''Intermédiarie des Recherches Mathématiques''. In 1948 Gérardin started publishing the journal ''Diophante'' and continued with it until his death.<ref name=BoyerPreface/>

In 1949, Paul Belgodère, the director (from 1949 to 1986) of the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]], purchased the important mathematical library that Gérardin had accumulated at Nancy.<ref name=BoyerPreface/>
